newsitem.title: NIGERIA: SOCCER-HUNGARIAN CONNED OVER NIGERIAN MANAGER JOB.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HUNGARIAN CONNED OVER NIGERIAN MANAGER JOB.

text.p: Former Hungarian team manager Kalman Meszoly has been duped by a Nigerian who said he would help him get the job of manager for the reigning Olympic soccer champions, the Nigerian Football Association (NFA) said on Tuesday.
Meszoly, a former Hungarian international, paid $2,000 to a Nigerian who had promised to submit his application and professional resume to the NFA.
Later the Nigerian allegedly told Meszoly he had been shortlisted for the job and demanded an unspecified amount of money as a commission fee.
The NFA dissociated itself from Meszoly's application in response to inquiries from the Hungarian through his country's embassy in Lagos.
"We are not aware of his application and he is working with a fake agent," NFA's spokesman Austin Mgbolu told reporters on Tuesday.
A statement from the Hungarian embassy in Lagos the previous day suggested Meszoly might have fallen victim to fraudsters.
Nigerian sports ministry officials said in December they had contacted "high-profile" names abroad to interview as a replacement for former manager Jo Bonfrere.
The Dutchman quit his position after leading Nigeria to a historic gold medal win in soccer at the Atlanta Olympics.
He had complained of poor treatment and interference in his duties by Nigerian sports authorities. 071730 GMT jan 97
